titre: Child support and your tax return
resume: The paying parent can deduct child support, the receiving parent declares it. With shared residence, no deduction but the tax shares are split. In Mayotte, a 40% income tax reduction also applies.
aQuoiCaSert: Child support paid for a child affects both parents' income tax: a deduction for one, taxable income for the other. It never appears on the pre-filled tax return: each parent must enter it themselves. Declaring it correctly, with the right proof, avoids mistakes and tax reassessments (redressements).
quiEstConcerne: The parent who pays support for a minor child who lives with the other parent.
The parent who receives the support.
The parent raising their children alone (box T).
aSavoir: Paying parent, minor child: support is deductible if the child usually lives with the other parent and is not counted in your family quotient (quotient familial, the system of tax shares per household). Costs related to your visiting rights are not deductible.
Receiving parent: support is taxable up to the amount the other parent can deduct. Declare it under "Pensions alimentaires perçues". A 10% allowance is applied automatically.
Shared residence: no support is deductible. Each child counts as a 1/4 share for each parent for the first two, then a 1/2 share from the third child.
Box T (case T): a single, divorced or separated parent who lives alone with their dependent children ticks box T and gets an extra half share.
Adult child not attached to your tax household: support is deductible up to €6,855 per child, with the child declaring the amount received.
Mayotte: income tax for households domiciled in Mayotte is reduced by 40%, up to €4,050 (article 197 of the code général des impôts, the French tax code).
In 2026, the online filing deadline for Mayotte was June 4 (départements 55 to 976).

documents.detail: Ask the court registry (greffe), the lawyer or the notary for a copy if you no longer have it.

documents.libelle: Proof of each payment during the year
documents.detail: Bank statements, transfer notices. Cash without a receipt is hard to prove.

documents.libelle: Invoices for expenses paid directly for the child
documents.detail: Schooling, medical costs, if you deduct them on top of the support.

documents.libelle: Annual summary of amounts paid or received
documents.detail: You can export it from the Lien Parental Journal.

documents.libelle: Decision or agreement setting the residence (shared or not)
documents.detail: To justify the split of shares or box T if the tax authorities ask.

etapes.titre: Add up the amounts paid or received over the calendar year
etapes.detail: The Journal (Finances filter, Pension category) gives you the history of recorded payments.

etapes.titre: Check before filling in your tax return
etapes.detail: The total matches your bank statements; the child is not declared as your dependent if you deduct the support; with shared residence you deduct nothing.
As deductible expenses if you pay it, under "Pensions alimentaires perçues" if you receive it.

etapes.titre: Tick box T if you are raising your children alone
etapes.detail: Only if you live alone with them and are single, divorced or separated.
The tax authorities may ask for it.
